monthly_review.summary: This month shows increased aerobic stimulus and improved pacing consistency, but with a notable drop in cadence and efficiency compared to last month. The shift toward higher-intensity zone distribution reflects intentional training progression.
monthly_review.highlight: Cadence dropped sharply from 150 spm last month to 141 spm this month — the largest absolute change across all metrics and a likely contributor to reduced stride length and increased ground contact time.

goal_tracker.message: You need 0.5 more km across up to 4 remaining sessions — achievable with one short 0.6 km recovery jog or integrated into a warm-up/cool-down.

insights.title: Efficiency improved despite slower average pace
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency rose from 13.28 to 13.35 km/hr per bpm, indicating better cardiovascular economy — especially notable given the 8 sec/km slowdown in average pace, suggesting improved HR management at sub-threshold efforts.

insights.title: Significant shift toward higher-intensity zones
insights.body: Zone 3+ time increased from 49% (z3+z4+z5 = 36+12+1) last month to 53% (26+17+5) this month, while Zone 1 dropped from 4% to 23% — reflecting intentional inclusion of easy runs but also a 20-percentage-point jump in Zone 3 specifically, which may signal early fatigue accumulation.

insights.title: Cadence-stride tradeoff emerging
insights.body: Cadence fell 9 spm (150 → 141) while stride length in faster runs (e.g., 91.78 cm on 2026-04-22) remained high — but ground contact time increased from avg 298 ms (Apr 22) to 314 ms (Apr 17) and 327 ms (Apr 26), suggesting compromised neuromuscular coordination during fatigue or low-effort runs.

insights.title: Lowest-effort run shows form breakdown
insights.body: The 14:00 min/km run on 2026-04-26 had cadence of only 87 spm, HR of 120 bpm (well below Z1), and ground contact of 327 ms — indicating passive shuffling rather than active recovery, likely impairing tissue resilience and gait patterning.

recommendations.action: Replace your next scheduled easy run with a 4 km Zone 1–2 run at HR ≤135 bpm and cadence ≥145 spm, using metronome or audio cue if needed.
recommendations.reason: Cadence dropped 9 spm this month and the slowest run showed severe form degradation (87 spm); rebuilding neuromuscular rhythm at low intensity will reinforce efficient turnover without fatigue.

recommendations.action: Perform 3 × 1-min strides at 4:28 min/km (best pace) after an easy 3 km warm-up, focusing on landing under center of mass and maintaining 148–152 spm.
recommendations.reason: Your best pace (428 sec/km) occurred during a 5 km run with 146 spm and 306 ms ground contact — replicating that turnover under controlled conditions will reinforce race-relevant mechanics.

recommendations.action: Skip any planned run on one of the remaining 4 days and instead complete 10 min of dynamic mobility + 5 min barefoot calf/foot drills on grass.
recommendations.reason: Ground contact time increased across recent runs (311 → 314 → 327 ms), and vertical oscillation spiked to 8.8 cm on 2026-04-22 — signaling reduced stiffness and potential fatigue; non-running stimulus will support tendon resilience.

weekly_focus.description: Re-establish efficient cadence and ground contact patterns through targeted low-fatigue stimuli — prioritizing rhythm, posture, and spring-like recoil over volume or intensity.
suggested_sessions: 4 km Zone 1–2 rhythm run (HR ≤135, cadence ≥145 spm)
